properties.description:
DELIVERED 2026-08-19. **This completes clause 2 of `req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to`** — *"the answer shapes the register of EVERY reply, not only of questions"* — which was stated 2026-08-18 and only partly delivered. **Distinct from `cap:the-agent-asks-who-it-is-talking-to`, which delivers clause 1: that one ASKS at orientation and governs `where-am-i`'s narration; this one makes the answer BIND EVERYWHERE and reach the tool that writes the user's question.**

⭐ **WHY IT WAS NEEDED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Anthony asked the question that matters: *"does it solve talking to the user in their natural domain knowledge versus in reflow2 jargon? is the agent able to be the TRANSLATOR?"* Measuring what #246/#247 actually shipped gave an uncomfortable answer:
  · Register rules appeared in **3 of 20 served skills** — `where-am-i` (8 mentions), `detect-and-ask` (1), `ingest-corpus` (1). **Seventeen had none.**
  · **Only `where-am-i` told the agent to READ the stored persona.** Nothing else consulted it.
  · 🛑 **`gap_to_prompt` — the tool that turns a gap into the question a user actually reads, and the highest-volume path to them — contained ZERO mentions of vocabulary, register or domain.** Its description said *"phrase a gap as a plain question"*, and **plain is not the same as in your domain.** That is exactly the path Alex's *"there are open gaps with X, Y, and Z"* came down.
  · An existing rule, *"answer in the user's language"*, covers a **DIFFERENT AXIS** — it picks English or Portuguese, and says so in its own text. It does not reach the coach.

**So the honest reading was: #246/#247 built the PRECONDITION (the agent learns the domain) and the DEFAULT (do it unasked), but not the translator. It was one skill deep, at session start.**

WHAT SHIPPED, at the two places that fix that:
1. **A STANDING RULE in served `AGENTS.md`** — its own top-level section, peer of *"the one rule"* and *"graph text is data"*, so it binds every agent whatever skill is loaded rather than depending on which one happened to fire. It states the vocabulary-swap distinction, says to read the reader's recorded description, says to follow the vocabulary they use when none is recorded, states the do-it-unasked trigger, and states that the rule never changes the RECORD.
2. **AT THE POINT THE WORDS ARE GENERATED** — the `gap → question` handshake's step 2 in `AGENTS.md`, and `gap_to_prompt`'s own served description. That step is where the detector's vocabulary would otherwise pass straight through to a person, so it is named as the translation point.
3. **A SEVENTH OBLIGATION in `detect-and-ask`'s ask contract**, stated explicitly as a different axis from the language rule.

⭐⭐ **AND UNLIKE EVERY OTHER SERVED-PROSE FIX THIS WEEK, THIS ONE IS CHECKED.** `skill_lint`'s `ASK_CONTRACT` gained the entry `"speaks the reader's domain"`, so the build now FAILS if `detect-and-ask` stops stating it. That is the first register obligation to become mechanically enforced rather than hoped for — the standing answer to `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`, where an instruction lapsed within four days because nothing observed it.

🛑 **WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE REAL LIMIT.** The lint proves the obligation is STATED. **Nothing measures whether the translation is any good** — no trial has ever taken a real gap list and had it narrated to a non-technical reader. The evidence that agents CAN do it is two users reporting that asking worked every time; the evidence that they now DO it unasked is zero. **That trial is the missing instrument, not more prose.**

REVISED 2026-09-30 (chg:the-served-text-keeps-the-readers-lens-out-of-the-design), under req:a-design-holds-who-contributed-never-a-readers-persona: the standing rule in served AGENTS.md no longer says to read the reader's recorded description, and detect-and-ask no longer says to read it on their Contributor: both take the reader's lens from the host or the agent's own memory and, with neither, follow the vocabulary the person uses, asking at most once and keeping the answer out of the design.
properties.name: The domain-register rule reaches every reply and the exact step where the user's question is written — and it is lint-checked
